profile.description: Held-out shape: four BF16 resident batches M32/H64/F192, FP32 accumulators and nonlinear/residual arithmetic, BF16 stage boundaries, all outputs/state on 16 PEs.

timing_protocol.scope: whole four-batch chain including all FP32 accumulations, BF16 conversions, arithmetic, movement, nonlinear/residual and every intermediate/output/state store

memory.scope: bin/*.elf program objects; not union of all ELF loads or physical area

research.hypothesis: Remove the separate FP32 row accumulator: accumulate expansions in res_tile, transpose via dead W1 after all transfers complete, and copy back before protected BF16 stage stores. For Mt=1 the two layouts coincide. Vector activation reuses res_tile for polynomial output and W1 for squares, then FP32 U; mixed BF16 G*0.5 with FP32 FMA restores the linear SiLU term without another tile. Guard both uses by 2*Mt<=Ht. This trades a timed extra pack pass for lower program memory, preserving every term, precision boundary, frame and state store.
research.falsification: Reject skipped/reordered projection terms, BF16 accumulation, missing stage quantization, stale logical reads, numerical/state/shutdown failures, protected-control changes, speedup below 1.05x or memory above 1.10x. Require six families, fresh matched seed and complete suite guards for cross-shape claims. Reject any alias used while communication is live or any scratch extent exceeding W1; compare complete working-state histories at both seeds. Reject any transpose-before-transfer completion, scratch extent beyond W1, missing copy-back, incorrect identity-layout case or missing original G in the mixed FMA. Require complete four-shape full/fresh memory and worst-cell gates before widening the claim.
